author: reek
body: Ray-traced soft shadows as a [Device] compute kernel. The same three-sphere, checkered-floor scene, lit by an overhead AREA light: each pixel that sees a surface casts a 3x3 grid of shadow rays toward points spread across the light disk and averages the visibility, so shadows have a soft penumbra instead of a hard edge. This is the reference site's "ray traced shadows" technique, from Codex [Device] AST. The soft-shadow sampler and the per-sample occlusion test are tail-recursive folds the plug lowers to nested WGSL loops. Real math from Gpu chapter DeviceMath.

author: reek
body: Light samples: a 3x3 grid across a disk at height 6, radius ~1.1.

author: reek
body: Fold over the 9 light samples, counting how many are visible from the hit point (each is a normalized shadow ray toward that light-disk point). The disk is centred at (lx, 6, lz), which orbits with the frame so the shadows sweep.
